name: Queensland
summary_text: Queensland is a protective outlier on the legal side: first in Australia to criminally prohibit conversion practices — Public Health Act 2005 ch 5B (s.213F), in force 20 August 2020, covering practices aimed at changing or suppressing sexual orientation or gender identity, with named prohibited techniques — and it drafted a complete anti-discrimination rewrite (Anti-Discrimination Bill 2024) with a modernised 'gender identity' attribute aligned to the Yogyakarta Principles, separated from sex-characteristics provisions, plus vilification offences; the rewrite was still in consultation in the documents reviewed. The one operationally adverse fact for a detained visitor is custody placement: Queensland sits outside the four self-identification jurisdictions (NSW, Victoria, ACT, Tasmania), so prison placement turns on surgical-intervention status or case-by-case assessment — meaning 'some trans women can be placed in men's prisons' here, unlike in the self-ID states.
